name: Open in a terminal app
summary: Open any session in the terminal app you already use (Ghostty, iTerm2, Terminal, Kitty, WezTerm or a command you confirm), drag a Finder folder onto the Dock icon to open it as a project, drop a file on a terminal to type its path, and reveal a session's folder in Finder or your editor.
where: Session menu, Open In Terminal App... in the menu bar, and the terminal widget menu, open in terminal app.
The Carnivore icon in the Dock (drop a folder) and any terminal in the window (drop a file or folder).
Session menu and File menu: Reveal in Finder, Open in Editor, Reveal Project in Finder, Open Project in Editor.
how_to: Pick your terminal app in settings, desktop app; Open In Terminal App... then opens the session there through its attach command.
Choose a custom command and Carnivore shows it in full and asks you to confirm the first time and whenever it changes.
Drag a folder from Finder onto the Carnivore icon in the Dock: it opens that project, or asks to add the folder as a project first.
Drag a file or folder from Finder onto a terminal: its quoted full path is typed at the prompt, not sent, so the agent can read it.
Session menu, Reveal in Finder or Open in Editor open the folder of the session in view; the editor is the default editor set in Settings, General.
examples: Watch an agent in Ghostty while Carnivore keeps the session alive.
Drop a screenshot onto a terminal so the agent can read its path.
Drop a project folder on the Dock icon to start working in it.
media_exempt: native: opens other macOS apps and takes Finder drops, which no browser capture can show
